findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile option (a) with the static per-request settings seam: cache_settings is one object handed to the FallbackModel and cannot be re-selected per answering candidate, so applying the primary's provider-specific cache keys would send Bedrock keys to an Anthropic fallback (a hard 400). Specify how (a) avoids this — e.g. gate cache-key application on the fallback actually NOT being able to fire, or confirm the pydantic-ai FallbackModel strips/rewrites per-provider settings — or adopt option (b).
evidence: Plan: 'intersect capabilities only over providers that can actually serve the current call (primary first; fallback capabilities apply only after a fallback)'
runner.py:518-522 builds cache_settings ONCE from intersected caps; runner.py:556-558 folds it into a single model_settings object passed to the Agent/FallbackModel
capabilities.py:688-691: 'Bedrock REJECTS a top-level cache_control outright ("Extra inputs are not permitted")'; anthropic_cache and bedrock keys are mutually exclusive

runner_support.py:55-58 docstring: collapsing disagreeing prompt-cache styles to 'none' is intentional because 'each style's keys are provider-specific and would error on the candidate that does not share it'
findings.finding: The preferred option (a) — 'intersect capabilities only over providers that can serve the current call (primary first)' — is unsound as literally stated because prompt-cache settings are applied via a SINGLE per-request `model_settings`/`cache_settings` object (runner.py:518-522, 556-558) handed to the FallbackModel, while which candidate answers is chosen at call time; applying the primary's Bedrock cache keys means an Anthropic fallback candidate receives Bedrock keys, which the provider hard-rejects ('Bedrock REJECTS a top-level cache_control outright', capabilities.py:688-691). That is the exact hazard the current collapse-to-none deliberately prevents (_intersect_capabilities docstring, runner_support.py:55-58: each style's keys 'would error on the candidate that does not share it').
scenarios: A mixed [bedrock:opus, anthropic:opus] chain where the Anthropic fallback fires: request carries Bedrock cache keys, provider 400s on the fallback path — an outage introduced precisely when the primary is degraded

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record on the ticket the existing cc33/dd27 rationale (and the LangChain#37042 prior art the code cites) for collapsing mixed cache styles to "none", and show how the chosen option honors it — specifically, where cache settings would be re-resolved per answering candidate given that model_settings is built once (runner.py:518-558) and the FallbackModel switches candidates transparently inside pydantic-ai.
evidence: runner_support.py:57-58 docstring: 'Disagreeing prompt-cache styles collapse to "none" for the same reason: each style's keys are provider-specific and would error on the candidate that does not share it.'

capabilities.py:682-691: 'PROVIDER ASYMMETRY — the trap. The two arms must use their OWN keys' — Anthropic top-level cache_control is REJECTED by Bedrock ('Extra inputs are not permitted'); pydantic-ai raises UserError if both Anthropic keys are set. Code cites LangChain#37042 as the same regression.

Web-retrieved prior art (LangChain reference + langchain-ai/langchain-aws#723, langchain#33635) confirms Anthropic vs Bedrock prompt caching are separate provider-specific middleware mechanisms — cache keys do not cross the provider boundary.

The plan's Approach names option (a) as the default and cites only 'the comment in rebar.toml' — it never names the cc33/dd27 collapse-to-none rationale it is reversing, so the reader cannot tell whether the fix respects the constraint that produced the current behavior.
findings.finding: Option (a) reverses a deliberate, documented design (task cc33 / bug dd27) that collapses mixed prompt-cache styles to "none" precisely because provider-specific cache keys are mutually exclusive and error on the wrong provider — yet the plan does not engage this recorded prior art (in-repo rationale + the LangChain#37042 regression the code cites) before committing to reverse it.
scenarios: A mixed [bedrock:opus, anthropic:opus] chain where the primary (Bedrock) cache keys get baked into model_settings, then a runtime fallback routes the call to the Anthropic-direct candidate — the Bedrock keys (or absence of Anthropic top-level cache) reach the wrong provider and 400.
Reviewer/author evaluating option (a) without the in-repo rationale and cannot judge whether it re-introduces the exact cross-provider error the collapse was designed to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, add a prior-art paragraph naming the cc33/dd27 collapse-to-none design and the provider-key asymmetry (Anthropic top-level anthropic_cache vs Bedrock bedrock_cache_messages, mutually exclusive; LangChain#37042). Then require the investigation to answer whether cache settings CAN be re-resolved at the moment a fallback answers — if not (settings are baked once into the FallbackModel), prefer option (b) homogeneous chains, which sidesteps the cross-provider-key hazard entirely.

evidence: Plan lists both options but defaults to (a) with only a hedge ('unless it destabilises the provider seam')

Codebase shows (a) touches the settings/routing seam (runner.py + runner_support.py + provenance) whereas (b) is confined to rebar.toml — a smaller blast radius given the mutually-incompatible provider keys
findings.finding: Given the concrete provider-incompatibility mechanism, option (b) (homogeneous chains in rebar.toml) is a structurally-different alternative that avoids the cache-key-crossing hazard entirely, yet the plan defaults to (a) 'unless it destabilises the provider seam' without weighing that (a) requires re-architecting where/when provider-specific settings are applied (per-candidate rather than per-request), whereas (b) is a config-only change with a smaller blast radius. The plan should either give a positive rationale for preferring (a) over (b) that accounts for the per-request-settings constraint, or reorder the default toward (b).
findings.location: Approach section — 'Default to (a) unless it destabilises the provider seam.'
scenarios: Implementer follows the stated default and pursues (a), then discovers mid-build that per-candidate cache settings are not expressible at the current seam
